sn46.2:1.2: For the phrase “sustained by food” see [dn33:1.8.2](), [an10.27:10.5](), [an10.28:4.5](), [kp4:1.2]() and notes. The word _āhāra_, literally “intake”, may be translated as “food” or “fuel” depending on context.
sn46.2:1.3: This passage can be seen as an expansion of the fourth _satipaṭṭhāna_, “observation of principles”, where the “principles” underlying the rise and fall of the hindrances and awakening factors are investigated. Similar teachings recur throughout this section, for example [sn46.51]().
sn46.2:2.2: “Feature of beauty” is _subhanimitta_. In early Pali, _nimitta_ is used for a feature or quality of the mind that, when focused on, promotes the growth of similar or related qualities. Thus focusing on beauty fosters the desire for that beauty. (See [mn5:6.1]()).
sn46.2:2.3: “Irrational” attention sees the beauty as something to be held on to and appropriated. The flaw lies not in the object, but in the response.
sn46.2:5.2: Worrying about anxiety makes the mind even more anxious.
sn46.2:6.2: Such as what the nature of the correct path ([an3.65:3.8]()), the various wrong views ([sn24.1:5.1]()), the status of a saint after death ([sn44.9:5.2]()), or the reality of kamma ([sn42.13:21.2]()).
sn46.2:9.2: These include the meditations listed in the Satipaṭṭhana Sutta ([mn10]()).
sn46.2:10.2: Discrimination between good and evil is the foundation of wisdom. | The phrase _sappaṭibhāgā_, which appears here in a stock phrase, is given three mutually exclusive explanations in the commentary (see Bodhi’s note on this sutta). I think the commentary is influenced by the later sense of _paṭibhāgā_ as a technical meditation term meaning “counterpart”. This sense is, however, absent from Sanskrit, where _pratibhāga_ means “portion, share” (Rig Veda 8.99.3, Manu 8.307). The sense would then refer to individuals “with a portion” of dark or bright qualities. This is, in fact, the theme of the only other passage in Pali that uses this term ([an6.62:10.2]()).
sn46.2:12.2: These are the things that bring wholesome joy to the mind, in and out of meditation.
sn46.2:14.2: The includes peaceful meditations such as mindfulness of breathing.
sn46.2:15.2: This includes the development of absorption, which is the basis for the equanimity of the fourth absorption, as well as the development of insight into attraction and repulsion (see [mn152]()).
